title: Brazil's census postponement: what the archived homepage establishes
finding: An extracted archive of IBGE's English homepage, captured on 30 March 2020, contains a notice dated 17 March stating that the census planned for 2020 was moved to 2021. This confirms an announced change of plan, not that enumeration actually took place in 2021.
why_it_matters: A revised census plan changes expected data availability. Keep the announcement date, revised plan and eventual completion date separate.
evidence_limit: The archived homepage establishes the announced revised plan. It does not establish the eventual enumeration year or the detailed reason for the postponement.

title: Japan's household survey: revised forms and a comparability warning
finding: A Statistics Bureau notice dated 9 March 2018 says revised account books were introduced to half the sampled households in January. It warns about discontinuities in annual changes and contributions, provides an adjustment using propensity scores and inverse-probability weighting, and records retrospective recalculation on 8 February 2019.
why_it_matters: When comparing household spending across the change, distinguish raw and adjusted figures and their vintages before interpreting a movement as a behavioural change.
evidence_limit: The official explanation documents the change and adjustments. This issue does not reconstruct every historical download or date the first public availability of each version.

title: Greece suspended the GDP flash release, while provisional data remained scheduled
finding: On 4 August 2017, ELSTAT suspended its GDP flash release at 45 days after the quarter and cancelled the second-quarter flash scheduled for 14 August. The same note kept provisional second-quarter data scheduled for 1 September. This is a suspension of the flash publication, not of all GDP statistics.
why_it_matters: Different releases of one indicator have different availability. A generic GDP stoppage label would misstate which information was missing.
evidence_limit: The notice distinguishes the withdrawn flash estimate from the still-scheduled provisional release. It does not prove the actual later publication date.

title: South Africa resumed insolvency statistics with an explicit series break
finding: Stats SA says its first resumed monthly insolvency release was published on 21 July 2026, covering June and including a series from January 2023. It explicitly identifies a gap from September 2021 to December 2022 and says the release is not a continuation of the earlier series. Liquidation statistics continued separately.
why_it_matters: Resumed publication does not automatically restore a complete continuous series. Distinguish insolvencies of individuals and partnerships, liquidation statistics and the stated gap when joining observations.
evidence_limit: The article supports resumed publication and an explicit series break. It does not establish the timing of every earlier missed release or the subsequent publication cadence.

title: Three surveys, two quarters: six reports under one catch-up episode
finding: In an archived PBOC index captured on 9 July 2024, all six third- and fourth-quarter 2023 reports for the depositor, entrepreneur and banker surveys carry a 22 March 2024 posting label. Six preserved official report pages show the same date.
why_it_matters: Reference periods and posting labels are different dimensions. Keeping both helps distinguish the period measured, the date displayed by the publisher and historically evidenced visibility, while avoiding three independent-disruption counts for a shared episode.
evidence_limit: The displayed posting date is not independently proven first public accessibility. The archive establishes presence by July 2024. The exact due date and delay length remain unconfirmed.

title: Two receivables-definition changes: similar names, different measures
finding: The NBS industrial-profits release dated 27 March 2019 explains that monthly accounts receivable was replaced that year by the combined notes-and-accounts-receivable measure. The release dated 27 March 2020 explains a switch back to accounts receivable. Both tie the adjustment to alignment with enterprise financial-statement formats.
why_it_matters: These measures should not be joined solely because their names are similar. Recording the definition and the release version in which it changes helps users assess comparability across time.
evidence_limit: The official releases establish two definition substitutions. This is not a check of every historical value or back series. The two changes remain separate events.

title: A collective-enterprise breakdown ended; the aggregate releases continued
finding: The NBS industrial-value-added release dated 14 March 2019 and industrial-profits release dated 27 March both state that the collective-enterprise breakdown would no longer be published from 2019. Both releases still contain their respective aggregate results, so the event concerns withdrawal of a registration-type breakdown.
why_it_matters: Users comparing a business category over time need to know when its public breakdown ends. Distinguishing that breakdown from continuing aggregates avoids overstating the data gap.
evidence_limit: The named breakdown disappears from these releases while aggregate figures continue. That does not establish absence from every other publication channel.
